candidate_requirements.requirement: Clarify the collapse pattern, circumstances and associated symptoms.
candidate_requirements.rationale: The positional opening alone does not establish a mechanism.
candidate_requirements.acceptable_alternatives: Witness/prodrome/recovery enquiries count even though detailed replies are absent.

candidate_requirements.requirement: Review medicines and the timing of the dose change.
candidate_requirements.rationale: A medicine-related hypothesis requires checking exposure rather than assuming it.
candidate_requirements.acceptable_alternatives: General medicine/recent-change questions count; missing drug/dose details must not be treated as a failed request.

candidate_requirements.rationale: Cardiac alternatives remain relevant in an older adult with collapses; this rationale does not depend on knowing the hidden infarction/device details.
candidate_requirements.acceptable_alternatives: A broad personal medical-history question is acceptable. Do not require guessing a pacemaker or requesting interrogation before learning it exists.

candidate_requirements.requirement: Request existing orthostatic blood-pressure or relevant cardiac observation/ECG evidence.
candidate_requirements.rationale: The proposed postural mechanism needs evidence or an acknowledged gap.
candidate_requirements.acceptable_alternatives: Lying/standing BP, ECG/rhythm or relevant examination enquiries are alternative routes. Unavailable results do not make a request inadequate.

candidate_requirements.requirement: Seek living arrangements or available support for the safety plan.
candidate_requirements.rationale: Support may affect implementation of advice after collapse.
candidate_requirements.acceptable_alternatives: Ask about living alone, available help or equivalent practical support.
